title: What if Galaga and Centipede became a 3D arcade shooter? My AI-assisted Unity demo
author: Illustrious-Lake2603
selftext:
I'm building INFEST around that idea: swarms, weapon pickups, high scores and boss fights, with FPS/TPS aiming. This is 25 seconds from me playing the Windows demo through a Boss Arachnia.



The workflow is Unity with Claude Code and Codex for coding and tooling, plus my own Maya work and some AI-assisted art. Most of the art I made myself.



One thing that's helped with AI debugging is giving it runtime evidence instead of just describing what looked wrong. Our in-game bug reports bundle screenshots with the camera pose, scene hierarchy, game state and recent logs. That gives the coding assistant an object and context to investigate. A snapshot still isn't a reproduction, so the fix needs another playtest.



I've also released Voxel Studio for anyone interested in voxel workflows: [https://github.com/cronobjs/voxel-studio](https://github.com/cronobjs/voxel-studio)



It's a local 3D voxelizer/editor with painting and sculpting tools, palette/shader previews, OBJ/GLB/FBX exports, and an optional MCP bridge. You're free to use and modify it for your own projects, including commercial games, under Apache-2.0. The core editor needs no AI subscription or API key. The README has setup steps and a screenshot. Imported models still need to be yours or properly licensed.



Free browser and Windows demos: [https://panic-blazeit.itch.io/infest-the-arcade](https://panic-blazeit.itch.io/infest-the-arcade)



Can you track what you're aiming at when the effects get busy? And for other Unity devs using AI: what runtime information has helped your assistant diagnose bugs? Happy to discuss the game or tool workflow.
